answer.reason: The Nile figures in several events of the story: Pharaoh's dream, the infant Moses laid by its bank, and the plague that turned its water to blood.

clauses.english: was where Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat cows and seven lean cows coming up
clauses.quote: there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed

clauses.english: was where the infant Moses was laid in an ark of bulrushes
clauses.quote: she laid it in the flags by the river's brink

clauses.english: was turned to blood by Moses and Aaron, and its fish died
clauses.quote: all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood

doubts: Left out the marked verses in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos, Nahum and Zechariah: they use the river as a figure, speak of drying up, or concern other rivers (No, Euphrates, Tyre's Sihor harvest) and are not events of the Nile itself.
EXO 17:5 only mentions the rod that smote the river; EXO 8 frogs and EXO 1:22 (boys cast into the river) were left out as lesser or as steps within other events.
